sources.label: measured / derived / approximate / unconfirmed as noted

distance_definition.supervisor_risk_quantity: clearance = min over obstacle-center positions predicted for the next 1.0 s (0.1 s steps, observed velocity) of the point-to-segment distance to the segment [robot current position -> current route target]; risk when clearance < stop_distance_m
distance_definition.consequence: stop_distance_m=1.1/1.38 are thresholds on a predicted center-to-path clearance, not on robot-obstacle center distance or surface gap

brake_envelope_measured.note: piecewise-linear interpolation used for approximate estimates

derived.definition: threshold applies to the reconstructed predicted path clearance, not to center distance or surface gap
derived.note: two decompositions kept separate to avoid double counting: (i) measured stop distance from the STOP trigger already contains the transport delay; (ii) brake_final4 distance starts at actuation, so v0*action_delay is added explicitly.  Both add closing*age + envelope radii.  Not strict worst cases.

ttl_over_criterion_c.queue_order_note: monotonic dispatch: an expired arrival is always issued after the current active setpoint, so the active has necessarily expired too; simultaneous applied residual on the rejection row is impossible. Residual evidence is the APPLIED rows immediately before the first rejection plus the expiry->NONE transition.

ttl_applicability.note: with a 50 ms control tick the arrival age quantizes to 0/50/100/150 ms; 150 ms equals the TTL and is rejected, so only <=100 ms transport delay is usable at TTL=150 ms.

labels.reconstructed_clearance: derived from raw rows (replay + case trajectory)
